subject: POC environment options & success criteria — NovusAI
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@novusai.com>
Cc: trial-eng@novusai.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC environment options & proposed success criteria

Olivia — great meeting earlier. Quick recap and a concrete recommendation so we can unblock the trial kickoff: 

1) Environment options (tradeoffs & recommended path)
- Hosted Redwood API (fastest): spinning up a scoped API key and preset model profiles. Pros: live in ~24 hours, no infra lift, lower operational lead time. Cons: shared hosting, data residency relies on regional controls. Recommended as initial ramp.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): isolated tenant with predictable throughput. Pros: closer to production parity, token cost lower at scale. Cons: provisioning 3–5 business days for GPU reservation.
- VPC/private deployment: customer-managed VPC + Private control plane. Pros: full isolation, KMS/HSM integration, auditability for regulated data. Cons: longer lead time (2–3 weeks typical), networking/config coordination required.

2) Proposed success criteria for the 2-week POC (what NovusAI said matters)
- Latency: 95th pct < 350ms for typical 512-token prompts using the selected model variant.
- Cost: endpoint unit cost <= target X (we'll model after you share sample traffic).
- Functional: paraphrase/QA accuracy above your baseline on the 50-case prompt set you shared.
- Stability: no more than 1 outage >5 minutes during the run window.

3) Immediate next steps & ownership (proposed)
- Marcus Lin (me): finalize scope, send trial plan doc and PO/contract checkbox items. (Today)
- Karthik Iyer (solutions): prepare sandbox provisioning checklist & estimate for dedicated/VPC (by EOD tomorrow)
- Marissa Cole (CS): draft evaluation rubric and data ingestion steps for your staging data (by Monday)
- Olivia / NovusAI: confirm starting environment (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) and provide sample prompt set + expected concurrency. (reply)

I've attached a short POC plan matrix (novusai-poc-plan.xlsx) that maps tests to owners/timeline. If you're comfortable, we recommend starting with the hosted trial to validate functional criteria while we parallelize dedicated/VPC gating items.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute follow-up if that helps.

—Marcus

Marcus — thanks for the tight recap. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the hosted route: 

(1) Data residency / encryption: does the hosted option give us region-locked storage and support our Azure KMS? We need to understand if any customer data lands outside our control for audit purposes.
(2) SOC 2 evidence: can you share the SOC 2 summary and the scope for hosted vs private? Our security lead will want that before sending any sample data.
(3) Timeline/cost for dedicated sandbox vs hosted: you mentioned 3–5 days vs 24 hours — can you provide an estimate table or rough delta on monthly cost so we can evaluate budget impact?

If hosted is quick and SOC 2 + region lock are acceptable, we can start with hosted for the 2-week functional run and evaluate migration to dedicated afterwards. We expect to have our security lead (CIO looped) review the SOC docs today.

Thanks — Olivia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC environment options & proposed success criteria

Olivia — hi, Karthik here (Solutions). Quick technical clarifications: 

- Hosted trial: we can provision scoped API keys and sample model profiles within 24 hours once we have the account owner and approved NDA. Data residency: hosted endpoints can be pinned to a cloud region (us-west-2 or eu-west-1) and we support encryption-at-rest with our managed keys. If you need Azure KMS specifically, that is only available on Private/VPC deployments.

- Dedicated sandbox: reservation and GPU assignment typically 3–5 business days (depends on quota and current capacity). Cost: expect ~1.8–2.5x per-token cost improvement relative to hosted at scale (depends on model & quantization). I'll attach a short VPC/network checklist for your network team.

- VPC/private: lead time 2–3 weeks (network approvals, peering, KMS setup). Required inputs: CIDR ranges, allowed egress rules, and KMS ARN if using AWS KMS. See attached vpc-network-checklist.pdf.

Staging dataset guidance: for the 2-week run, a 500–1,000 prompt sample with expected concurrency numbers is sufficient to hit latency and stability targets. We recommend read-only ingestion to avoid accidental writes during evaluation.

Quick sample of the API binding we'll give you for hosted trial (example):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <DEMO_KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"<your prompt>","max_tokens":512}'

I'll follow up with a one-page cost delta table this afternoon.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
